heading: Comedy & Live Shows in the Okanagan, Fall & Winter 2026–27
title: Okanagan Comedy & Live Shows 2026–27 | Okanagan Roam
description: John Mulaney, Jim Jefferies, Ron James, Come From Away, Frozen and more: stand-up, musicals, drag and family shows in the Okanagan, 2026–27.
intro: This guide gathers the comedy, theatre and live shows coming to the Okanagan from late October 2026 through spring 2027: big-name stand-up at Prospera Place, comedy nights in pubs and breweries, dinner-theatre musicals, drag brunches and shows the whole family can enjoy. At the end, there are places to eat near the main theatres.
Each item shows its town and date. Shows sell out, and dates sometimes move, so check the event page before you buy tickets.

items.name: John Mulaney: Mister Whatever Tour
items.text: the four-time Emmy-winning comedian brings his new stand-up tour to Prospera Place. The show has been rescheduled; tickets already bought are valid for the new date.

items.name: Jim Jefferies – Son of a Carpenter Tour
items.text: the Australian comedian blends observational comedy about growing up as a carpenter's son with his famously no-topic-off-limits take on modern life, at Prospera Place. He's known for Netflix specials including Two Limb Policy, the FX series Legit and The Jim Jefferies Show.

items.name: Ron James: The Noise Between Our Ears
items.text: Ron James's new stand-up show takes on politics south of the border, Baby Boomers twenty years from 'the home' and life as a tech-challenged adult, plus classic bits on hand-me-down hockey gear and camping trips with pals. Tickets in Oliver are $82.50. Also in {event:vernon/ron-james-the-noise-between-our-ears|Vernon, Oct 29} and {event:kelowna/ron-james-the-noise-between-our-ears-live|Kelowna, Oct 30}.

items.name: Danny Bhoy Live
items.text: the Scottish comedian returns on his ninth cross-Canada tour with Dear World…, a stand-up and theatre hybrid, at Kelowna Community Theatre. Tickets are about $68–79.

items.name: Alex Mackenzie's Hungry for Laughs Comedy Tour
items.text: a stand-up lineup with Alex Mackenzie, Ola Dada, Brittany Lyseng and Efthimios Nasiopoulous, comics seen on Just for Laughs and CBC's The Debaters. Every ticket supports local charities. Also in {event:kelowna/hungry-for-laughs-comedy-tour-kelowna|Kelowna, Oct 24}.

items.name: James Mullinger
items.text: the British-born, Canada-based comedian tours a new stand-up show built on his outsider's take on Canadian life, at Venables Theatre.

items.name: Snowed In Comedy Tour (Vernon)
items.text: the long-running winter stand-up tour, now in its 18th year, brings a lineup of Canadian comedians to the Performing Arts Centre.

items.name: Brent Butt
items.text: the creator and star of Corner Gas performs stand-up in his laid-back, storytelling style, at Venables Theatre.

sections.heading: Comedy nights in pubs, breweries and clubs

items.name: Next Stop Comedy at Three Lakes Brewing
items.text: a monthly stand-up night at Three Lakes Brewing, with a new lineup of touring and local comics each show.

items.name: Sergei Putinski – Russia's Only Living Comedian (Tonics Pub)
items.text: Train Wreck Comedy presents the viral character comic known for the tracksuit-and-brick-phone act. Tickets are $35.

items.name: Train Wreck Comedy: All-Stars at The Hub on Martin
items.text: three touring BC stand-up comics share the bill in downtown Penticton. Early-bird tickets cost less.

items.name: Derek Seguin - Train Wreck Comedy
items.text: Montreal's Derek Seguin, an 11-time performer at the Just For Laughs Festival, at Kelowna Actors Studio.

items.name: Maple Laughs Comedy Show at the Barley Mill Brew Pub
items.text: a touring stand-up show featuring Canadian comics, with a different lineup each time and the occasional surprise act.

items.name: Sick & Twisted Comedy Night
items.text: a dark comedy night at Dakoda's Comedy Lounge headlined by Kyle Lucey, with local comics. Not for the easily offended.

items.name: Ben Albert: Live in Penticton at the Barley Mill Brew Pub
items.text: the stand-up comic brings his touring show to the Barley Mill for a late-evening set.

items.name: Next Stop Comedy at Unleashed Brewing
items.text: stand-up comedy at Unleashed Brewing in the North End, including a New Year's Eve show.
items.where: Kelowna, Dec 31 and one more date

items.name: Damonde Tschritter at Kelowna Actors Studio
items.text: the Canadian stand-up headlines one of the studio's stand-up comedy weekends.
items.where: Kelowna, Jan 15 and one more date

items.name: Hassan Phills: Live in Kelowna
items.text: the fast-rising Canadian stand-up brings new material and his crowd-work style to Rustic Reel Brewing, with a 9:30 pm show.

items.name: Lachlan Patterson – Train Wreck Comedy
items.text: the veteran Canadian stand-up brings his laid-back, offbeat style to the Rotary Centre for the Arts.

items.name: The Art of Magic & Illusion with Ryan Michael Magic
items.text: close-up magic and an interactive stage show of mind reading, illusions and comedy in the Crown & Thieves speakeasy. A fun, intimate date night.
items.where: West Kelowna, several dates from Oct 25

items.name: God Is a Scottish Drag Queen: Halloween Spooktacular (Vernon)
items.text: Mike Delamont's hit comedy character, God in a power suit and Scottish accent, returns with a Halloween-themed show. For adults.

items.name: THE COMIC STRIPPERS! at the Cleland Theatre
items.text: a male stripper parody and improv comedy show, semi-undressed and completely unscripted, with no extreme nudity. It won a Canadian Comedy Award for best live production. Strictly 19+. Also in {event:vernon/the-comic-strippers-19-only|Vernon, May 14}.

items.name: TAWANAN Night: Filipino Comedy
items.text: a night of stand-up and sketch comedy from well-known Filipino comedians, open to everyone who likes a laugh.

items.name: Comedy Hypnosis Show at SilverStar
items.text: comedy hypnotist Gavin Hooper brings his clean, interactive show to the NATC auditorium, where volunteers from the crowd become the stars.

items.name: Couples Clownselling: Love Is a Joke
items.text: a Valentine's Day comedy in which clown 'counsellors' poke fun at couples and romance. Ages 16 and up.

items.name: Hyprov: Improv Under Hypnosis
items.text: audience volunteers are hypnotized and then perform improv comedy alongside a professional improviser. Best for adults and teens.

items.name: Wheeler Walker Jr.: Pullin' Out Farewell Tour
items.text: comedian Ben Hoffman's raunchy country-singer character plays a farewell tour show. Explicit humour; strictly for adults.

items.name: Little Shop of Horrors
items.text: Actors Studio stages the cult-classic musical as a dinner-theatre night. Expect rock, Motown and dark comedy with plenty of camp. Tickets are $82.

items.name: Bury the Hatchet
items.text: a touring play retelling the Lizzie Borden axe-murder case of 1892. Dark, gripping theatre for the Halloween season.

items.name: "The Dinner Theatre" Live
items.text: a world-premiere musical about two Broadway veterans reunited at a dinner theatre in Moncton, written by and starring Canadian recording artist Rick Worrall. Despite the title, no dinner is served.

items.name: Every Christmas Story Ever Told (and Then Some!) – Many Hats Theatre
items.text: three actors refuse to do A Christmas Carol yet again and race through every holiday story and TV special they can think of instead. It runs four weekends with evening and Sunday matinee shows.

items.name: Disney's Frozen the Musical
items.text: Kelowna Actors Studio's holiday-season production, Wednesday to Saturday at 7 pm with weekend matinees. Doors open at 5:30 pm for dinner before evening shows; food is extra. Many shows are close to selling out.

items.name: Anne of Green Gables
items.text: New Vintage Theatre's annual holiday play, with a cast of local talent in an all-ages production, at the Rotary Centre for the Arts.

items.name: Le Hockey Sweater
items.text: Caravan Farm Theatre's winter show is a joyful, raucous take on Roch Carrier's Canadian classic The Hockey Sweater, bringing an outdoor hockey game to the farm's fields and forests.

items.name: Palliser Suite: Two One-Act Comedies at Powerhouse Theatre
items.text: two award-winning one-act comedies set in Calgary's Palliser Hotel, in the spirit of Neil Simon. Light, quick and very funny.

items.name: Come From Away
items.text: the Tony Award-winning musical tells the true story of Gander, Newfoundland, which took in nearly 7,000 stranded passengers on September 11, 2001. Evening shows Wednesday to Saturday plus weekend matinees; tickets $93–$100.

items.name: Clue: On Stage at Powerhouse Theatre
items.text: the board game becomes a fast farce. Expect slapstick, rapid-fire jokes and plenty of whodunit twists.

items.name: VDPAC Presents: Louisa May Alcott's LITTLE WOMEN
items.text: an Arts Club Theatre Company production of Little Women. Tickets in Vernon are $49–$59, including fees. Also in {event:oliver/little-women-arts-club-theatre|Oliver, Mar 31}.

items.name: Chicago The Musical
items.text: the roaring-twenties musical, with a Bob Fosse-style score including “All That Jazz” and “Cell Block Tango”. Tickets are $93–$100.

items.name: Bunnicula - The Musical
items.text: a colourful family musical at The Balsam School. The show runs about 60 minutes and suits all ages.

items.name: Magician Leif David Magic Show
items.text: award-winning magician Leif David presents a family-friendly show of close-up and stage magic with clean comedy. Tickets are $18 including fees.

items.name: Luminarium: Juggling Saves the World
items.text: physical theatre with juggling and clowning. Wordless, playful fun for kids and adults.

items.name: Harlem Globetrotters: Rivalry Tour
items.text: trick-shot basketball and comedy routines at the South Okanagan Events Centre, on a tour marking 100 years of the team.

items.name: Yuki the Juggler
items.text: Yuki Ueda blends traditional and modern juggling with freestyle dance, clowning and theatre. Tickets are $18, including fees.

items.name: The Wilds by Wonderheads
items.text: a wordless mask-theatre adventure. Gentle, magical storytelling for families.

items.name: Roald Dahl's Willy Wonka – TYA (Pixie & Dot)
items.text: a family-friendly youth-theatre version of Willy Wonka, with golden tickets, Oompa Loompas and the classic songs.

items.name: Magic! at Creekside
items.text: three Canadian magicians mix magic, comedy and audience participation for an age-diverse crowd. All seats are $49, including fees and taxes.

items.name: Ella's Naughty Drag Brunch
items.text: Ella Lamoureux and a rotating cast of drag performers host a brunch at the Unicorn Lounge. Admission is $10; reserve your spot.

items.name: Ella's Naughty Drag Bingo at The Hub on Martin
items.text: a bawdy, adults-only bingo night with cheeky prizes and nonstop jokes. 19+.

items.name: Drag Brunch with Joan & Janice
items.text: a Sunday drag brunch at Unicorn Lounge starring Joan & Janice Everyday, an intergalactic duo of alien queens. Admission is $10.

items.name: A Freida Whales Drag Show
items.text: an intimate drag show in The Broken Hearts Club speakeasy at Crown & Thieves. It's a 19+ event; tickets are $40.

items.name: Ken's Kings Night: 2nd Anniversary Showcase
items.text: a drag king cabaret celebrating two years of Kelowna's Ken's Kings Night, in the intimate Black Box Theatre.

items.name: WAR on the Catwalk: Drag Race Tour
items.text: stars from RuPaul's Drag Race and Canada's Drag Race, hosted by Alyssa Edwards, compete in a glam runway show.

items.name: Kelowna Community Theatre
items.text: a city-run, roughly 850-seat theatre in the Cultural District, with a smaller Black Box space for cabaret and intimate shows.

items.name: Rotary Centre for the Arts
items.text: a community arts hub with the 326-seat Mary Irwin Theatre hosting comedy, concerts and film.

items.name: Vernon & District Performing Arts Centre
items.text: Vernon's main performing arts venue, with a 750-seat auditorium. Tickets for every show are sold through Ticketseller.ca.

items.name: Powerhouse Theatre
items.text: an award-winning community theatre in one of Vernon's historic buildings.

items.name: Cleland Community Theatre
items.text: the city-run, 443-seat theatre inside the Penticton Community Centre on Power Street. Most tickets are sold through ValleyFirst Tix.

items.name: Venables Theatre
items.text: a 400-seat theatre with an on-site lounge and free parking.

items.name: Creekside Theatre
items.text: a 250-seat community theatre hosting touring musicians, comedy, dance and magic shows in an intimate room.

sections.heading: Dinner before the show
sections.lead: Well-rated places to eat a short walk from the main stages: Kelowna's Cultural District (Kelowna Community Theatre, the Rotary Centre for the Arts and Prospera Place), Vernon's Performing Arts Centre, Penticton's Cleland Theatre and Oliver's Venables Theatre.

items.name: King Taps
items.text: a lakeside patio, a well-reviewed happy hour menu and a big cocktail list.

items.name: Soul De Cuba Cafe
items.text: an authentic Cuban restaurant on Sunset Dr. Order the ropa vieja poutine and the croquettes.

items.name: Skinny Duke's Glorious Emporium
items.text: a retro '70s-themed lounge. Order a spread of shareable Asian-fusion small plates and an inventive cocktail.

items.name: Pizza Garden
items.text: a wood-oven pizza shop with a celiac-safe process.

items.name: HUMO Kelowna
items.text: an intimate tasting-menu restaurant, a good pick for a first date or special occasion. Book ahead.

items.name: Intermezzo Restaurant and Wine Cellar
items.text: an elegant Italian restaurant, with live Spanish guitar on select nights.

items.name: Kawakubo Vernon
items.text: a Japanese restaurant whose dining room is filled with art.

items.name: Pizzeria Tratto Napoletana
items.text: order a Neapolitan pie; the non-alcoholic beer options are tasty too.

items.name: Savvios Family Restaurant
items.text: Greek-Italian comfort food in generous portions. The souvlaki and spanakopita are the dishes locals come back for.

items.name: Auntie Ag's Seafood Cafe
items.text: a tiny, no-frills cafe focused on fish and chips.
